::: {#sol-bikeshare-ratio}

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

##### R

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
# The rate ratio for a 0.1 rise in temp is exp(0.1 * coefficient of temp).
ratio_r <- exp(0.1 * pois_coef[["temp"]])
round(ratio_r, 3)
```

##### Python

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
import numpy as np

# The rate ratio for a 0.1 rise in temp is exp(0.1 * coefficient of temp).
ratio_py = float(np.exp(0.1 * pois_py.params["temp"]))
round(ratio_py, 3)
```

:::

```{r}
#| include: false
ratio_r_round <- round(ratio_r, 2)
ratio_py_round <- round(reticulate::py$ratio_py, 2)
```

By @thm-poisson-rate-ratio with $a - b = 0.1$,
the [rate ratio](poisson-regression.qmd#def-rate-ratio) is $\expf{0.1 \coef{\text{temp}}}$,
and its [estimate](estimation.qmd#def-estimate) is $\expf{0.1 \hcoef{\text{temp}}}$.
That estimate is `r ratio_r_round` in the R tab and `r ratio_py_round` in the Python tab,
so the [estimated](estimation.qmd#def-estimate) [event rate](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/distributions.html#def-event-rate) of the warmer hour is about `r ratio_r_round` times that of the cooler hour.

:::
